summary: This is a preliminary U.S. Code page for 12 USC Chapter 4, Taxation, part of Title 12 (Banks and Banking). It lists the chapter's four subchapters and the text of the surviving sections: exemption of Federal Reserve banks from taxation (§531), the tax on national bank circulating notes (§541), and state taxation of national bank shares (§548). It also gives codification, amendment and repeal notes, including the 1969 amendment and the historical end of national bank note circulation in 1935.
one_line: Preliminary text of 12 U.S.C. Chapter 4 on taxation, covering Federal Reserve bank tax exemption, national bank note taxes, and state taxation of national bank shares.
key_facts: 12 USC Chapter 4 is titled TAXATION and falls under Title 12, Banks and Banking.
Section 531 exempts Federal reserve banks, including their capital stock, surplus and income, from Federal, State, and local taxation, except taxes upon real estate.

Section 541 requires every association to pay the Treasurer of the United States a duty of one-half of 1 per centum each half year on the average amount of its notes in circulation, paid in January and July.
Section 548 provides that for tax law purposes a national bank is treated as a bank organized and existing under the laws of the State or jurisdiction where its principal office is located.
Section 542 related to a tax on circulating notes secured by 2 per centum bonds and was enacted by act Mar. 14, 1900.
Section 543 was repealed by Pub. L. 97–258, §5(b), Sept. 13, 1982, and related to circulating notes secured by Panama Canal 2 per centum bonds.
Sections 544 to 547 are omitted; they related to half-yearly circulation returns, penalties for failing to make returns, enforcing the circulation tax, and refunding excess tax.
The Pub. L. 91–156 amendment of Dec. 24, 1969 changed national bank share taxation provisions; the restriction removal was made effective January 1, 1973.
Pub. L. 93–100 §7 (Aug. 16, 1973) was cited as the State Taxation of Depositories Act and deferred certain State 'doing business' taxes on depositories.
Pub. L. 92–213 §4(b) (Dec. 22, 1971) required the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to study revenue impact on State and local governments and report within six months.

A February 17, 1941 Treasury communication stated that the retirement of the 2% Consols of 1930 and the 2% Panama Canal bonds ended National Bank note circulation and the collection of the tax thereon.
Sections 561 to 570 on state bank circulation were omitted, with their provisions incorporated into Title 26, Internal Revenue Code.
The page lists editions and supplements of the code from the 1994 Main Edition (1/4/1995) through the 2018 Edition and Supplement IV (1/5/2023).
